'''Patience Mthunzi-Kufa''' (born 2 May 1976) is a South African [[physicist]] and head of [[biophotonics]] research at the [[Council for Scientific and Industrial Research]]. She received the [[Order of Mapungubwe]] in Bronze.

== Early life and education ==
Patience Mthunzi-Kufa (Patience Mthunzi) was born on 2 May 1976, in [[Orlando, Soweto]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.thepresidency.gov.za/national-orders/recipient/dr-patience-mthunzi|title=Dr Patience Mthunzi {{!}} The Presidency|website=www.thepresidency.gov.za|language=en|access-date=2018-03-03|archive-date=11 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211111121643/http://www.thepresidency.gov.za/national-orders/recipient/dr-patience-mthunzi|url-status=dead}}</ref> She attended Reasöma Secondary School and enrolled for bachelor's degree in [[Psychology]].<ref name=":0" /> She became interested in [[Biology|biological science]], and switched majors, graduating from [[Rand Afrikaans University]] in 1999.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.csir.co.za/dr-patience-thenjiwe-mthunzi-kufa|title=Dr Patience Thenjiwe Mthunzi-Kufa {{!}} CSIR|website=www.csir.co.za|language=en|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref> At the same institution, she completed [[Postgraduate education|postgraduate degrees]] in [[Biochemistry]].<ref name=":1" /> She cites her aunt as inspiration: a teacher, and the only member of her family to complete a master's degree.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.brandsouthafrica.com/investments-immigration/science-technology/sa-scientist-forbes|title=South African scientist hailed as power woman|last=Mafika|date=2013-01-10|work=Brand South Africa|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en-US}}</ref>

Mthunzi began to work for the National Laser Centre in the [[Council for Scientific and Industrial Research]], where she set up a functional [[Cell culture|cell-culture]] facility.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.photonics.com/a51512/Ones_to_Watch|title=Ones to Watch|first1=Caren B.|last1=Les|first2=Karen A.|last2=Newman|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref> Whilst at a conference in [[San Diego]], Mthunzi-Kufa saw a presentation on [[optical tweezers]] which made her consider a career in [[biophotonics]]. It was not possible to study this in South Africa, so she moved to [[University of St Andrews]], where she was the first South African PhD student in the discipline.<ref name="Allemand">{{Cite web|url=http://www.yase-conference.eu/index.php/en/program/yase-at-the-science-forum-south-africa/94-interview-with-patience-mthunzi-kufa|title=Interview with Patience Mthunzi-Kufa|last=Allemand|first=Luc|website=YASE Conference|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref> She earned her PhD in 2010, "Optical sorting and photo-transfection of mammalian cells".<ref>{{Cite thesis|date=2010-11-30|others=Dholakia, Kishan, Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), South Africa, University of St Andrews|title=Optical sorting and photo-transfection of mammalian cells|language=en|hdl=10023/1254|publisher=University of St Andrews|type=Thesis}}</ref> She was a member of the [[SPIE]] students chapter in St Andrews.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spie.org/membership/student-members/student-chapters/student-chapter?chapter_id=1015542&SSO=1|title=Univ. of St. Andrews Chapter {{!}} SPIE Membership: SPIE|website=spie.org|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref>

== Career ==
As lead for [[biophotonics]] research at the [[Council for Scientific and Industrial Research]], Mthunzi users high power lasers to characterise and treat disease.{{citation needed|date=March 2018}} She uses lasers to optically manipulate cells at the microscopic scale, including:<ref name=":1" />
* Embryonic stem cells for tissue engineering<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mthunzi|first1=Patience|last2=He|first2=Kuang|last3=Ngcobo|first3=Sandile|last4=Khanyile|first4=Thulile|last5=Warner|first5=Jamie H.|date=2014-05-01|title=Graphene for improved femtosecond laser based pluripotent stem cell transfection|journal=Journal of Biophotonics|language=en|volume=7|issue=5|pages=351–362|doi=10.1002/jbio.201300028|pmid=23996967|s2cid=205980180 |issn=1864-0648}}</ref> 
* Neuroblastoma cells for neurodegenerative studies
* HIV-1 cells for targeted drug delivery in latent viral sites 
* Cancer cells to study single cell processes
She visited [[Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology]] to discuss ''Biomedical Applications of Lasers in Biophotonics'' in 2013.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://groups.oist.jp/light/event/seminar-dr-patience-mthunzi-biomedical-applications-lasers-biophotonics|title=Seminar by Dr. Patience Mthunzi 'Biomedical Applications of Lasers in Biophotonics' {{!}} OIST Groups|website=groups.oist.jp|access-date=2018-03-03|date=2013-10-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://groups.oist.jp/light/post/2013/10/16/dr-patience-mthunzi-csir-south-africa-visits-lmi-unit|title=Dr Patience Mthunzi CSIR, South Africa visits LMI Unit {{!}} OIST Groups|website=groups.oist.jp|access-date=2018-03-03|date=2013-10-16}}</ref>

In 2015, Mthunzi was appointed a [[TED Fellow]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ted.com/speakers/patience_mthunzi|title=Patience Mthunzi {{!}} Speaker {{!}} TED|last=Mthunzi|first=Patience|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en}}</ref> Her TED talk, ''Could we cure HIV with lasers?'', has been viewed over one million times.<ref>{{Citation|last=Mthunzi|first=Patience|title=Could we cure HIV with lasers?|date=14 August 2015 |url=https://www.ted.com/talks/patience_mthunzi_could_we_cure_hiv_with_lasers/up-next|language=en|accessdate=2018-03-03}}</ref> She used the opportunity to discuss wish to translate her research from petri dishes to human testing.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://blog.ted.com/giant-pouched-rats-baby-corals-the-fbi-a-recap-of-tedfellows-session-2-at-ted2015/|title=Giant pouched rats, baby corals & the FBI: A recap of TEDFellows Session 2 at TED2015|date=2015-03-17|work=TED Blog|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/technology-31749754|title=Eighteen minutes to change the world|last=Wakefield|first=Jane|date=2015-03-16|work=BBC News|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en-GB}}</ref> Her talk was well received by the audience in Vancouver and scientists all over the world.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hivequal.org/on-health/removing-hiv-with-laser-beams-the-sci-fi-treatment-that-just-might-work|title=Removing HIV With Laser Beams: The Sci-Fi Treatment That Just Might Work|website=www.hivequal.org|language=en|access-date=2018-03-03|archive-date=4 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304055253/http://www.hivequal.org/on-health/removing-hiv-with-laser-beams-the-sci-fi-treatment-that-just-might-work|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.medicalbag.com/tech-talk/tedxtalk-could-we-cure-hiv-with-lasers-patience-mthunzi/article/571296/|title=TEDxTalk: Could We Cure HIV with Lasers? {{!}} Patience Mthunzi|date=2016-11-07|work=Medical Bag|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://curebylaser.tumblr.com/|title=A Cure for HIV?|website=curebylaser.tumblr.com|language=en|access-date=2018-03-03|archive-date=27 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627162524/https://curebylaser.tumblr.com/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Mthunzi is concerned about the brain drain of African scientists out of South Africa.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfsa.co.za/come-back-how-africa-attracts-its-young-scientists/|title=Come Back: How Africa Attracts Its Young Scientists – SFSA|website=www.sfsa.co.za|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-03|archive-date=4 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304055311/http://www.sfsa.co.za/come-back-how-africa-attracts-its-young-scientists/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Allemand"/> In 2014 she spoke at Girlpower UNISA.<ref>{{Citation|first=Nkululeko|last=Mpakama|title=Girlpower UNISA Dr Patience Mthunzi|date=2014-06-20|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FWmTSA1wq8E|accessdate=2018-03-03}}</ref> In 2016 she appeared on [[SABC 2]] ''Visionaries' Lounge.''<ref>{{Citation|title=Visionaries' Lounge - Episode 19: Dr Patience Mthunzi-Kufa|date=2016-02-22|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ur3nwBrv2Hk|accessdate=2018-03-03}}</ref> She has also appeared on ''Moves and Shakers.''<ref>{{Citation|title=Movers&Shakers {{!}} Dr Patience Mthunzi (Episode 19)|date=2013-05-22|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vcgc8fy3AcA|accessdate=2018-03-03}}</ref> She was featured on [[CNBC Africa]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnbcafrica.com/tag/patience-mthunzi/|title=Patience Mthunzi Archives - CNBC Africa|website=CNBC Africa|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref> She is a contributor to Talking Heads, an African speakers platform for change-makers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://talkingheads.org.za/speakers-tags/dr-patience-mthunzi/|title=Dr Patience Mthunzi Archives - Talking Heads|website=Talking Heads|language=en-US|access-date=2018-03-03|archive-date=4 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304172330/http://talkingheads.org.za/speakers-tags/dr-patience-mthunzi/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Mthunzi is co-chair of the South African Young Academy of Science.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sayas.org.za/?team=patience-mthunzi|title=Patience Mthunzi-Kufa - SAYAS|work=SAYAS|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ekon.sun.ac.za/ebwresearch/Research/Blog/Entries/2013/7/8_Call_for_nominations_to_the_South_African_Young_Academy_of_Science_(SAYAS)_is_now_open_files/South%20African%20Young%20Academy%20of%20Science-%20Background%20Information.pdf|title=Background Information - SAYAS|last=|first=|date=|website=Department of Economics at Stellenbosch University|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref> She is helping the Young African Scientists in Europe (YASE) with their 2018 meeting, dedicated to African early career researchers.<ref>{{Citation|title=Patience Mthunzi-Kufa: from Soweto to Scotland and back again / de Soweto à l'Ecosse, et de retour|date=2018-02-01|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XMcuKIe29Ik|accessdate=2018-03-03}}</ref>

In 2022, Dr. Mthunzi-Kufa was appointed as the Deputy Chairperson of the Advisory Council on [[Orders, decorations, and medals of South Africa|National Orders]] by [[President of South Africa|South African President]] [[Cyril Ramaphosa]].<ref>
{{cite web
|url=https://www.csir.co.za/dr-mthunzi-kufa-appointed-deputy-chairperson-advisory-council-on-national-orders
|title=Dr Mthunzi-Kufa appointed as the Deputy Chairperson of the Advisory Council on National Orders
|date=24 February 2022
|website=CSIR
|access-date=17 October 2022
}}
</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
* 2011 – Selected to participate in the IAP/[[World Economic Forum]]'s [[World Economic Forum|Summer Davos]] conference in Dalian, China<ref name=":1" />
* 2012 – [[Order of Mapungubwe]] in Bronze, awarded by [[Jacob Zuma]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thepresidency.gov.za/national-orders/order-mapungubwe-0|title=The Order of Mapungubwe {{!}} The Presidency|website=www.thepresidency.gov.za|language=en|access-date=2018-03-03|archive-date=11 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211111120632/http://www.thepresidency.gov.za/national-orders/order-mapungubwe-0|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pressreader.com/south-africa/sunday-times/20120429/281646777146900|title=Zuma honours SA's heroes|via=PressReader|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref>
* 2012 – [[SPIE]] One to  Watch<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://spie.org/about-spie/press-room/spie-member-news/ones-to-watch-8-2-12|title=SPIE Members Working in Optical Science Are 'Ones to Watch'|website=spie.org|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref>
* 2012 – [[Forbes magazine]] Ten youngest power women in Africa<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.standardmedia.co.ke/article/2000073955/ten-youngest-power-women-in-africa|title=Ten youngest power women in Africa|work=The Standard|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/mfonobongnsehe/2012/12/06/the-20-youngest-power-women-in-africa-2012/#24cc3dd011e3|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121209012026/http://www.forbes.com/sites/mfonobongnsehe/2012/12/06/the-20-youngest-power-women-in-africa-2012/#24cc3dd011e3|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 9, 2012|title=The 20 Youngest Power Women In Africa 2012|last=Nsehe|first=Mfonobong|work=Forbes|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.globalblackhistory.com/2012/12/20-youngest-power-women-in-africa.html|title=20 Youngest Power Women in Africa - Global Black History|date=2012-12-17|work=Global Black History|access-date=2018-03-03|language=en-US}}</ref>
* 2012 – South Africa's Most Influential Women<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://whoswho.co.za/patience-mthunzi-436922|title=Patience Mthunzi {{!}} Who's Who SA|website=whoswho.co.za|language=en|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref>
* 2014 – Plenary speaker at the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] International Conference for Women in Physics<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://icwip2014.wlu.ca/indexd773.html?id=page&slug=plenary_speakers|title=ICWIP 2014|website=icwip2014.wlu.ca|language=en|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref>
* 2014 – Selected to the [[Global Young Academy]]
* 2014 – Emerging Leader at [[Genentech]], San Francisco
* 2017 – Selected to attend [[BRICS]] Young Scientist Forum in China, [[Zhejiang University]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.csir.co.za/drs-patience-mthunzi-kufa-and-angela-dudley-fly-csir-flag-high|title=Drs Patience Mthunzi-Kufa and Angela Dudley fly CSIR flag high {{!}} CSIR|website=www.csir.co.za|language=en|access-date=2018-03-03}}</ref>
